questions.question: A 16-year-old with primary amenorrhea has a 46,XY karyotype. Exam shows normal breast development, sparse pubic and axillary hair, and a short blind-ending vagina; no uterus is seen on ultrasound and intra-abdominal testes are found. Serum testosterone is elevated for age. Which structure is absent because of an intact Sertoli cell product?

explanations.A: Absent here, but because androgen signaling is lost, not because of a Sertoli product.
explanations.B: Prostate depends on DHT acting on AR; its absence reflects androgen insensitivity, not AMH.
explanations.C: Scrotal development is DHT-dependent, so it fails from AR loss, not from a Sertoli product.
explanations.D: Sertoli cells still secrete AMH, which regresses the Müllerian ducts, so no uterus or upper vagina forms.
explanations.E: Wolffian structures regress from lack of testosterone signaling, not from AMH.

questions.question: A newborn with a 46,XY karyotype has bilateral inguinal testes, a normal penis and scrotum, and at hernia repair is found to have a uterus and fallopian tubes alongside a normal vas deferens and epididymis. Which defect best explains these findings?

explanations.A: Would give undervirilized external genitalia (DHT-dependent) without persistent Müllerian structures.
explanations.B: Without AMH signaling the Müllerian ducts persist, while intact testosterone develops Wolffian ducts and a male phenotype.
explanations.C: Would cause regressed Wolffian ducts and female-appearing external genitalia, with Müllerian regression intact.
explanations.D: Would give immature gonads, regressed Wolffian ducts and a female phenotype.
explanations.E: Klinefelter has regressed Müllerian ducts; the karyotype here is XY.

questions.question: A 15-year-old girl with short stature and primary amenorrhea has a 45,X karyotype. Pelvic imaging shows a uterus and fallopian tubes but no identifiable ovarian follicles. Which gonadal and ductal pattern is expected?

answers.A: Immature testis; Müllerian regressed; Wolffian developed
answers.C: Streak gonad; Müllerian developed; Wolffian regressed

explanations.A: Describes Klinefelter or XX with SRY translocation.
explanations.B: Describes a normal XX individual; Turner gonads are streaks.
explanations.C: With no Y chromosome there is no SRY, so Müllerian ducts persist, Wolffian ducts regress and the gonad is a streak.
explanations.D: Describes XY with AMH signal deficiency.
explanations.E: Describes XY with impaired testosterone signaling.

questions.question: A phenotypically male infant with a 46,XX karyotype has small testes, no Müllerian structures and normal Wolffian derivatives. FISH shows Y-chromosome material on an X chromosome. As an adult, this patient is most likely to resemble which condition?

explanations.A: Would produce a female external phenotype from an XY karyotype.
explanations.B: XX with SRY translocation gives a phenotype similar to XXY: male, with immature, mostly sterile testes.
explanations.C: Testes in SRY translocation are immature and the patient is generally infertile.
explanations.D: Requires AMH deficiency; here Müllerian ducts regressed normally.
explanations.E: XO individuals lack SRY and have streak gonads and a female phenotype.

questions.question: A 13-year-old boy is evaluated for delayed puberty. He is given a continuous subcutaneous infusion of a GnRH analog as a diagnostic trial. After two weeks, which change in serum hormone levels is most likely?

answers.C: Increased FSH and decreased inhibin B
answers.E: Unchanged LH and markedly increased testosterone

explanations.A: Continuous GnRH desensitizes the pituitary and reduces LH release, so Leydig testosterone output falls.
explanations.B: Testosterone production depends on LH and cannot rise when LH falls.
explanations.C: FSH would also fall with pituitary desensitization; inhibin B would not drive this pattern.
explanations.D: This is the response to pulsatile, not continuous, GnRH.
explanations.E: LH is reduced by continuous exposure, and testosterone follows LH.

questions.question: A 24-year-old competitive weightlifter has been injecting testosterone for 6 months. Semen analysis shows severe oligospermia with sperm of normal morphology and motility. Which hormone pattern is most consistent with his findings?

answers.A: High LH, high FSH, high testosterone
answers.B: High LH, low FSH, low testosterone
answers.C: Low LH, high FSH, high testosterone
answers.D: Low LH, low FSH, high testosterone
answers.E: Normal LH, normal FSH, high testosterone

explanations.A: Exogenous testosterone suppresses rather than raises gonadotropins.
explanations.B: Does not match exogenous androgen use, which raises total testosterone.
explanations.C: FSH is also suppressed by negative feedback.
explanations.D: Exogenous testosterone suppresses LH and FSH by negative feedback, lowering sperm count even though plasma testosterone is high.
explanations.E: Negative feedback lowers both gonadotropins.

questions.question: A 30-year-old man with infertility has a seminiferous tubule disorder that selectively reduces germ cell number while Leydig cells are spared. Which change in serum hormones is expected?

answers.A: Decreased FSH and increased inhibin B
answers.C: Increased FSH and decreased inhibin B
answers.D: Increased LH and increased inhibin B
answers.E: Unchanged FSH and decreased inhibin B

explanations.A: Inhibin B falls, not rises, when germ cells are lost.
explanations.B: Leydig cells are spared, so the LH–testosterone loop is not primarily affected.
explanations.C: Fewer germ cells reduce Sertoli inhibin B, removing feedback on the pituitary so FSH rises.
explanations.D: Inhibin B tracks sperm count and would fall.
explanations.E: Inhibin B normally suppresses FSH, so its fall raises FSH.

questions.question: A researcher selectively knocks out the FSH receptor in adult mouse testes. Which Sertoli cell product would be expected to decline most directly?

explanations.A: FSH raises Sertoli cAMP, inducing inhibin B, growth factors, aromatase and ABP.
explanations.B: AMH is a fetal Sertoli product causing Müllerian regression, not the adult FSH-cAMP target listed in the lecture.
explanations.C: DHT is made by 5α-reductase in target tissues, not by FSH-stimulated Sertoli cells.
explanations.D: LH is a pituitary hormone.
explanations.E: Testosterone is made by Leydig cells in response to LH.

questions.question: A 26-year-old man with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism wishes to father a child. His testosterone is low and sperm count is near zero. Supplemental testosterone alone has not restored spermatogenesis. Which regimen is most appropriate to restore sperm production?

explanations.A: Not the lecture's described therapy; it does not supply the missing gonadotropins.
explanations.B: Continuous GnRH suppresses LH release.
explanations.C: FSH and hCG (as an LH substitute) restore Sertoli and Leydig activation and are used to treat testicular infertility.
explanations.D: Testosterone alone is not sufficient for spermatogonial proliferation and further suppresses gonadotropins.
explanations.E: Inhibin B would suppress FSH and worsen spermatogenesis.

questions.question: A 19-year-old XY individual has ambiguous genitalia at birth that virilized at puberty. He has normal epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicles, but a small prostate, sparse facial and body hair, and no acne. Which enzyme deficiency best explains this?

explanations.A: Would impair testosterone synthesis itself, affecting Wolffian structures as well.
explanations.B: Without DHT, prostate, external genitalia, body hair and sebaceous activity are underdeveloped while testosterone-dependent Wolffian structures are normal.
explanations.C: Would impair estradiol, causing delayed epiphyseal closure rather than poor prostate development.
explanations.D: Would abolish all steroidogenesis including Wolffian development.
explanations.E: Not involved in the lecture's androgen actions.

questions.question: A 25-year-old man is unusually tall with persistently open epiphyseal growth plates and low bone mineral density. Testosterone is elevated, while estradiol is undetectable. Deficiency of which enzyme is most likely?

explanations.A: Would impair DHT actions (prostate, external genitalia, hair), not bone maturation.
explanations.B: Without conversion of testosterone to estradiol, growth plates do not close and bone mass is not preserved.
explanations.C: Would abolish testosterone production as well.
explanations.D: Liver metabolism of androgens does not drive epiphyseal closure.
explanations.E: An adrenal enzyme; deficiency causes androgen excess but would not remove estradiol.

questions.question: A 70-year-old man reports decreased libido, fatigue and loss of muscle mass. Serum testosterone is low. According to the physiology of andropause, which pair of mechanisms underlies his decline?

answers.A: Increased aromatase and increased inhibin B
answers.C: Pituitary resistance to GnRH with compensatory FSH excess
answers.D: Reduced GnRH release and Leydig unresponsiveness
answers.E: Sertoli cell loss and increased ABP

explanations.A: Not the described mechanisms of andropause.
explanations.B: Not presented as causes of andropause in the lecture.
explanations.C: Not the mechanism described.
explanations.D: Andropause results from reduced hypothalamic GnRH release and loss of Leydig cell responsiveness to LH.
explanations.E: Sertoli function does not determine plasma testosterone.

questions.question: A 32-year-old man undergoes bilateral orchiectomy for trauma. Which fraction of his prior total circulating testosterone is he most likely to retain from peripheral conversion of DHEA and androstenedione?

explanations.A: 2% refers to the fraction of testosterone excreted in urine, not peripheral production.
explanations.B: 20% refers to the testicular share of total estrogen.
explanations.C: Leydig cells make about 95% of testosterone; about 5% comes from peripheral conversion of DHEA and androstenedione.
explanations.D: Peripheral tissues make only a small fraction.
explanations.E: This is the Leydig cell contribution, lost with orchiectomy.

questions.question: In a man with normal testicular function, testosterone concentration within the seminiferous tubule lumen is far higher than in plasma. Which mechanism best explains this?

explanations.A: Plasma binding transports testosterone to peripheral tissues, not into the lumen.
explanations.B: Aromatase reduces testosterone by converting it to estradiol.
explanations.C: ABP from Sertoli cells binds testosterone, which then cannot cross the blood–testis barrier and remains concentrated in the lumen.
explanations.D: Liver metabolism inactivates testosterone for excretion.
explanations.E: Peripheral tissues contribute only about 5% of testosterone.

questions.question: A 28-year-old man with infertility has bilateral undescended testes that were never corrected. Leydig cell testosterone output is adequate. What is the main reason for his impaired spermatogenesis?

answers.C: Failure of Wolffian duct development in utero
answers.E: Temperature above that tolerated by sperm

explanations.A: AMH acts on Müllerian ducts and does not affect adult spermatogenesis.
explanations.B: Inhibin B falls, not rises, with fewer germ cells.
explanations.C: Wolffian development depends on testosterone, which is adequate.
explanations.D: SRY is required for testis formation, which occurred.
explanations.E: Sperm will not mature at core body temperature, so cryptorchidism causes infertility.

questions.question: A 40-year-old man starts finasteride, a 5α-reductase inhibitor, for symptoms of an enlarged prostate. Which additional effect would be expected from reduced DHT action?

explanations.A: Growth plate closure is estradiol-mediated.
explanations.B: Male-pattern balding is a DHT action, so reducing DHT tends to improve it.
explanations.C: Sebaceous activity is DHT-driven and would decrease.
explanations.D: Wolffian structures depend on testosterone, not DHT.
explanations.E: Laryngeal growth is a testosterone action and is already established.

questions.question: A 62-year-old man undergoes radical prostatectomy with injury to the pelvic parasympathetic nerves. Which step of the male sexual response is most directly impaired?

explanations.A: Detumescence is sympathetically mediated.
explanations.B: Ejaculation is a striated-muscle reflex triggered by semen in the bulbous urethra.
explanations.C: Emission is sympathetically mediated.
explanations.D: Parasympathetic ACh stimulates endothelial NO, relaxing corporeal smooth muscle so the corpus cavernosum fills.
explanations.E: Internal sphincter contraction is sympathetic.

questions.question: A 55-year-old man taking an α1-adrenergic antagonist for urinary symptoms reports dry orgasms, and post-orgasm urine contains sperm. Failure of which mechanism best explains this?

explanations.A: The reflex that expels semen depends on semen reaching the bulbous urethra, which is downstream.
explanations.B: NO-mediated vasodilation governs erection, not antegrade ejaculation.
explanations.C: Sympathetic contraction of the internal sphincter normally blocks entry of semen into the bladder; loss causes retrograde ejaculation.
explanations.D: Testosterone does not control the immediate mechanics of emission.
explanations.E: Parasympathetic signaling drives erection.

questions.question: A 23-year-old man's semen analysis reveals oligospermia. A clinician wants to know how long after correcting the cause a new semen analysis will reflect a full cycle of sperm production. Which interval is closest?

explanations.A: This is the interval between successive waves of spermatogenesis, not the full maturation time.
explanations.B: This is the time for further maturation in the epididymis only.
explanations.C: This is sperm lifespan after ejaculation.
explanations.D: Longer than the maturation process described.
explanations.E: Maturation from spermatogonium to sperm takes about 70 days.

questions.question: A 12-year-old boy begins puberty. Which initiating event in the hypothalamus is primarily responsible for the rise in his plasma testosterone?

answers.A: Continuous high-level GnRH secretion from neurons
answers.B: Dis-inhibition of the GnRH pulse generator

explanations.A: Continuous GnRH reduces LH release.
explanations.B: Puberty starts when the suppressed GnRH pulse generator is released, producing pulsatile GnRH that drives LH and FSH.
explanations.C: Would lower, not raise, plasma testosterone.
explanations.D: Inhibin B is a Sertoli product that suppresses FSH.
explanations.E: Aromatase converts testosterone to estradiol and is not the initiating event.
